page0.text:
"Sakura."
She calls her name and throws it.

page1.text:
It's her greatest weapon.
She tosses the Magician's irreplaceable relic like she's playing catch.
"Welt, Ende. (Collapse phenomenon.)"
The cavern is flooded with light.

page2.text:
It explodes.
The Jeweled Sword embodying miracles that humans cannot achieve crumbles, erasing all shadow.

page3.text:
And then she runs.
Rin makes a beeline for Sakura.
Sakura freezes, cowering from the light.
She may have acquired great power, but she's still an amateur with zero combat experience.
If Rin wanted, it would be a simple matter to defeat her.

page4.text:
She easily closes the gap.
While running, she grips another knife she was hiding behind her back.

page5.text:
...
Sakura can't react.
She might have realized that she's about to die, but it's far too late.

page6.text:
...Rin's got her.
"It's over," she thinks, as she thrusts the knife—
Oh. I can't do this.
And she realizes her own defeat.

page7.text:
...I'm dead.
She realizes that it's too late to dodge, and that the knife is going to stab her in the heart.
She'll try a counterattack, but it won't stop it in time.

page8.text:
"She's...going to kill me."
She doesn't feel fear.
She's used to people hurting her.
It feels terribly natural that Rin Tohsaka is the one to do it.

page9.text:
But Sakura closes her eyes. She doesn't like pain, and she's afraid of dying.
She's relieved to know that if she disappears here, at least she won't suffer as much.

page10.text:
"...?"
But it doesn't hurt, and the end doesn't come.
Instead, she feels something very warm.
The moment Sakura notices where it's coming from,
her blinded vision returns.

page11.text:
...Someone's bleeding.
Warm human blood is trickling from her stomach.
Blood which can never be returned is flowing from her sister, who's hugging her tightly and seems like she's about to collapse.

page12.text:
"Nee...san?"
Why? The girl asks.
Rin was clearly faster.
Sakura was clearly about to be killed, but at the very end, the knife never stabbed her.

page13.text:
"...Oh, man. I can't rag on Shirou anymore, can I?"
She murmurs absently.
The girl always yearned for this.
It's the voice of the sarcastic and merciless, but warm and kind Rin Tohsaka.

page14.text:
Rin thinks...
...There really wasn't much to it.
In that last moment, she just felt that this was the best thing to do.
Once she saw Sakura up close, she felt like, "I can't kill Sakura, huh..."

page15.text:
"...Haah. I'm such an idiot."
...She's amazed at herself.
She really does have a knack for screwing up at the worst possible times, to have realized such a thing at the last possible moment.
Realize it sooner, you idiot.
But, well, it is what it is. Rin decides to accept it.

page16.text:
"...Yeah. It is what it is.
I can't leave sloppy people alone. I like it when things are done properly, so I can't stand it when people aren't rewarded appropriately for trying their best..."

page18.text:
"I love you, Sakura. I've always been watching, hoping that you'd smile... Yeah. I believed that maybe the harder my life was, the easier yours would be.
That's why I've never thought...that my life was hard."

page19.text:
She hugs Sakura lovingly.
It's the embrace of a lifetime, between sisters.
She gently hugs the sister who just ran her through the stomach, as if discovering a long-sought treasure.

page20.text:
"Nee...san..."
...Warmth leaves her body.
She doesn't complain.
Rin doesn't regret her death; only that she couldn't save her little sister.

page21.text:
"Sorry for being such a selfish big sister.
...But, thanks. I'm really happy that you wore the ribbon all this time."
Then, she collapses on the altar, like a falling red flower.

page22.text:
"...Ah."
Her weight is gone.
In that moment, her sister disappears along with that mirage-like warmth.

page23.text:
But Sakura, even though I'm this insensitive...
I've never once thought that I've lived a blessed life.

page24.text:
"...No."
How much loneliness was behind those words?
The girl's suffering was her own.
No one else could understand it or release her from it.
That hypocrisy wasn't possible.

page25.text:
In the same sense...
What if the sister she'd always looked up to and believed in was going through loneliness that nobody else could understand?

page26.text:
"I..."
What if that were true?
She was her ideal, who had everything she ever wanted and was always full of confidence.
What if her sister was always chained by something too?

page27.text:
"I..."
Then...
It would mean that the world wasn't weak and bad.
She was the only cowardly one for not looking up.
And there were people who awkwardly tried to love her.

page29.text:
...Where did I go wrong?
Everywhere.
I wanted it so badly, but it was right in front of me all along.
She hugged me so softly, and thought so much about me.
And I... I smashed it all to pieces, with my own hands.
